wheel.note: Cruiser Corps lists the same 15x5.5 OEM steel wheel for 1958–1990 FJ40, FJ45, FJ55, FJ60, FJ62 and BJ trucks, and advises against tires wider than 10.5 in on it.

items.title: Wiring campaign (1968–69 Land Cruisers)
items.summary: NHTSA lists a 1968–69 Land Cruiser electrical-wiring campaign covering 263 vehicles, but its online record carries no defect or remedy text and doesn't name the body style. Earlier write-ups describe mis-fitted door scuff plates chafing the harness; we couldn't re-verify that, so ask Toyota or check the harness under the sill plates yourself.

timeline.change: FJ45V four-door wagon (2,650 mm) launched alongside the short-wheelbase 40
2,950 mm long-wheelbase FJ45 pickup and cab-chassis added
FJ55 wagon launched in August with Toyota's first fully boxed frame, replacing the FJ45 wagon
HJ45 launched with the 3.6 L H diesel six; FJ55 gets revised side markers
4.2 L 2F and a four-speed replace the 3.9 L F and three-speed; FJ55 gets a domed hood (sold as the FJ56 in Japan)
FJ55 rear lamps move lower with integrated turn signals and reverse lights
FJ55 production ends in July; HJ47 and BJ45 arrive
End of J40-family production in Japan; Venezuela built long-chassis trucks until 8/1985

identify.intro: Long-wheelbase 40s came in a confusing spread of body and engine codes, and Brazilian Bandeirantes sometimes get sold as FJ45s or FJ55s.

items.head: FJ55 frame numbers
items.body: Owners date FJ55s from the frame number using Toyota production microfiche, for example frames 76441–77572 for July 1977. Some California titles carry an extra leading zero that isn't on the frame, so check that the numbers match.

items.head: FJ55 year tells
items.body: A center-domed hood means a 1975-or-later 2F truck; lower rear lamps with integrated turn signals mean 1978 or later. Two-tone paint and grille-set headlights are original.

items.head: FJ45 body codes
items.body: IH8MUD's J45 chart lists codes by body: FJ45V/FJ45L wagons (1961–67), FJ45P-B long-bed pickups (8/64–1/75), FJ45RP and FJ45LP pickups from 1975, and FJ45V/LV Troopies from 6/77. HJ45 and HJ47 are diesel sixes; BJ45 is the four-cylinder diesel.

items.head: Bandeirante isn't a 55
items.body: Brazilian Toyota Bandeirantes (OJ50/OJ55, later BJ50/BJ55) are 40-series derivatives with Mercedes-Benz or Toyota 14B diesels. An 'OJ55' is a Brazilian pickup or wagon, not an FJ55.

capability.v: 2,700 mm (106.3 in) FJ55 · 2,650 mm wagon / 2,950 mm pickup FJ45

values.intro: Long-bed FJ45 pickups and Troopies have overtaken FJ55s at auction, while stock FJ55s stay surprisingly affordable and LS-swapped restomods fetch big money.
values.note: Based on Bring a Trailer sales from January 2025 to October 2026: 18 FJ55s (median about $19,100, with LS3 and Vortec swaps at $42,500–$106,000) and 54 FJ45s, excluding Bandeirantes (median about $28,400; a 1965 SWB pickup made $122,000). Hagerty's FJ55 guide put the 2023 median at $34,500 and #2 condition at $46,300.

paragraphs: The US got gasoline FJ45s and FJ55s. HJ45, HJ47 and BJ45 diesels, right-hand-drive Troopies and Brazilian Bandeirantes are gray-market. A vehicle at least 25 years old, measured from its date of manufacture, can be imported into the US without meeting FMVSS, so every J40-family truck now qualifies. JDMBUYSELL notes that EPA still expects the original-design engine or an EPA-certified replacement. Corsetti Cruisers warns that California may refuse to register an import without a 50-state-compliant emissions system, so plan for that before buying a BJ or HJ.

production.intro: The FJ55 ran for 13 years as Toyota's first purpose-built station wagon, while the long-wheelbase 45 outlived it as a pickup and Troopy.
